explain.say: When you turn down the treble on a speaker, or a phone strips hiss from a recording, a filter is at work. The simplest is just a resistor and a capacitor. On the board, a 1 volt AC signal goes through a 1 kilohm resistor, and we take the output across a 159 nanofarad capacitor. This is a low-pass filter.

parts.label: R
parts.ask: What is the cutoff frequency of an RC filter?

parts.label: C
parts.ask: Why does the capacitor block high frequencies here?

explain.say: Think about the capacitor's reactance, 1 over 2 pi f C. At low frequency it is huge, almost an open circuit, so nearly all the input appears at the output. At high frequency it is tiny, almost a short, so the output collapses. Low notes pass, high notes are blocked, hence the name. What happens to a DC input?

draw.text: X_C = 1/(2πfC): large at low f, small at high f

explain.say: It passes completely. The changeover happens at the cutoff frequency, where the reactance equals R: f c equals 1 over 2 pi R C. Here that is 1 over 2 pi times 1 kilohm times 159 nanofarads, about 1 kilohertz. At cutoff the output is 0.707 volts, which is minus 3 decibels, half the power. Why half the power, if the voltage is 0.707?

parts.label: R
parts.ask: What is the cutoff frequency of an RC filter?

parts.label: C
parts.ask: Why does the capacitor block high frequencies here?

explain.say: Because power goes as voltage squared, and 0.707 squared is 0.5. This is the Bode plot: gain in decibels against frequency on a log scale, each step ten times the last. It is flat below 1 kilohertz, then falls steadily: at 10 kilohertz the gain is minus 20 decibels, a tenth of the voltage. What is the gain at 100 kilohertz?

curves.label: High-pass
curves.ask: How do you make a high-pass filter?

draw.text: On the x axis, 1 means 10 Hz, 3 means 1 kHz and 5 means 100 kHz.

explain.say: About minus 40 decibels. Now swap the two parts, capacitor in series and output across the resistor, and you get the mirror image: a high-pass filter that blocks low frequencies and DC. Same cutoff, same formula. Superb! Speaker crossovers use both, sending lows to the woofer and highs to the tweeter. Challenge: what resistor gives a 100 hertz cutoff with the same capacitor?

curves.ask: How do you make a high-pass filter?

faq.a: A circuit that lets low frequencies through and weakens high ones. The simplest is a series resistor with the output taken across a capacitor.
asks: How does an RC low-pass filter work?
What does a low pass filter do?

faq.q: What is the cutoff frequency of an RC filter?
faq.a: f c equals 1 over 2 pi R C. It is where the capacitor's reactance equals the resistance and the output has fallen to 0.707 of the input, which is minus 3 decibels.
asks: What is the minus 3 dB point?

faq.q: Why does the capacitor block high frequencies here?
faq.a: At high frequency the capacitor's reactance is tiny, so it shorts the output to ground. Most of the voltage is dropped across the resistor instead.
asks: Why does a capacitor short high frequencies?

faq.a: A decibel compares two powers on a log scale: 10 times the log of the power ratio, or 20 times the log of the voltage ratio. Minus 20 decibels means a tenth of the voltage.

faq.q: How do you make a high-pass filter?
faq.a: Swap the parts: put the capacitor in series and take the output across the resistor. Low frequencies and DC are blocked, high frequencies pass, with the same cutoff formula.

facts: A single RC filter stage rolls off at 20 decibels per decade, about 6 decibels per octave.
At the cutoff frequency the output voltage is 1 over root 2, about 70.7 percent, of the input.

quiz.say: R is 1 kilohm and C is 1 microfarad. What is the cutoff frequency?
quiz.show: R = 1 kΩ and C = 1 µF. What is the cutoff frequency?
quiz.why: R C is 1 millisecond, and 1 over 2 pi times 0.001 is about 159 hertz.

wrong.1: One over R C gives 1000 radians per second, not hertz; divide by 2 pi.
wrong.2: Check the powers of ten: R C is a thousandth of a second, not a millionth.

quiz.say: In an RC low-pass filter, what is the output taken across?
quiz.show: In an RC low-pass filter, the output is taken across...
quiz.why: The capacitor's voltage stays high at low frequency and falls at high frequency, which is low-pass behaviour.

wrong.1: Taking the output across the resistor gives a high-pass filter.
wrong.2: The source voltage is the input, not the filtered output.
